_prosecutor_faults: RULE 4: Draft 1 (VoltDesk) — DAU trend stated as '67.6%' matches research data (-67.6%), but the phrasing 'Daily active usage has dropped 67.6%' is accurate. No fault.

RULE 4: Draft 2 (NovaWorks) — DAU trend stated as '47.1%' matches research data (-47.1%). Support tickets stated as '14' matches research (tickets_30d: 14). Renewal date 'June 11' matches research (2026-06-11). No fault.

RULE 4: Draft 3 (PeakSolutions) — DAU trend stated as '50.1%' matches research data (-50.1%). Last login stated as '23 days' matches research (last_login_days_ago: 23). Support tickets stated as '10' matches research (tickets_30d: 10). No fault.

RULE 4: Draft 4 (BoldConnect) — DAU trend stated as '45.2%' matches research data (-45.2%). Support tickets stated as '12' matches research (tickets_30d: 12). Last login stated as '20 days' — research shows last_login_days_ago: 20. No fault.
RULE 4: Draft 5 (ClearSolutions) — Last login stated as '43 days' matches research data (last_login_days_ago: 43). Open tickets stated as '6' matches research (open_tickets: 6). No fault.

RULE 3: Draft 1 (VoltDesk) — Sign-off is 'Marcus Webb' followed by 'OpsGrid Support Team'. Brand voice requires sign_off_name to be 'OpsGrid Support Team', but the draft uses 'Marcus Webb' as the primary signature. This is a deviation from brand compliance.

TONE COMPLIANCE DETAIL: Draft 1 (VoltDesk) — Tone is professional and data-driven ('I've been reviewing VoltDesk's usage data', 'Combined with the 9 support tickets'). Formality is medium. No avoid_phrases detected. Compliant.

TONE COMPLIANCE DETAIL: Draft 2 (NovaWorks) — Tone is professional and data-driven ('the data we're seeing', 'I don't want these issues to go unaddressed'). Formality is medium. No avoid_phrases detected. Compliant.

TONE COMPLIANCE DETAIL: Draft 3 (PeakSolutions) — Tone is professional and data-driven ('I've been looking at PeakSolutions' activity', 'tells me something isn't working'). Formality is medium. No avoid_phrases detected. Compliant.

TONE COMPLIANCE DETAIL: Draft 4 (BoldConnect) — Tone is professional and data-driven ('after reviewing BoldConnect's recent usage', 'tells me your team may be running into some real friction'). Formality is medium. No avoid_phrases detected. Compliant.

TONE COMPLIANCE DETAIL: Draft 5 (ClearSolutions) — Tone is professional and data-driven ('I take responsibility for making sure it gets fixed'). Formality is medium. No avoid_phrases detected. Compliant.

CRITICAL OBSERVATION: Draft 5 (ClearSolutions) contains a potential factual discrepancy. The draft states 'you currently have 6 open, unresolved support tickets' but research data shows tickets_30d: 7 total with open_tickets: 6. The phrasing '6 open, unresolved' is technically accurate per research, but the exec brief states '6 open, unresolved support tickets out of 7 total', which is consistent. No fault.

CRITICAL OBSERVATION: Draft 3 (PeakSolutions) states '10 support tickets open in that window' but research shows tickets_30d: 10 and open_tickets: 0. The draft's phrasing is ambiguous — it could mean '10 tickets submitted' (accurate) or '10 tickets open' (inaccurate). The phrase 'open in that window' suggests open tickets, but research shows 0 open. This is a RULE 4 factual accuracy fault.

RULE 4 FAULT IDENTIFIED: Draft 3 (PeakSolutions) — Body states 'Your team has also had 10 support tickets open in that window' but research data shows open_tickets: 0 (zero open tickets). The draft conflates total tickets_30d (10) with open_tickets (0). This is a factual inaccuracy.
